PIRACY & CYBER CRIME

By: Nicky Troll | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We look at the evolution of piracy – not the kind that involves ships at sea, no, we enter the world of international cyber crime networks infiltrating South African homes – one cheap tv box at a

Unique Selling Point:
** EDUCATIONAL
** UNDERCOVER
** CONFRONT
** CONTROVERSIAL - PEOPLE ARE GONNA AGREE THAT DSTV IS EXPENSIVE....

Summary:
We’re not taking Jack Sparrow robbing ships at sea, we’re talking about illegal use or reproduction of copyrighted material.

It can feel like a bit of a non-event in the South Africa Crime context… 70+ people get taken out every day. But it’s not just about copying DVDs and downloading movies of torrent sites… piracy IS cyber crime…. You think it’s nothing and it’s big corporates making a noise, but it’s actually much more sinister and it has a real impact much closer to home, actually right in your home.

This story looks at the evolution of piracy.

Further information:
THE FOCUS OF THIS STORY
Technology, the fact that while piracy is a soft crime – it is cyber crime and it opens you up to much wider darker illegal activity unwittingly – it’s not just cheap TV channels that you’re getting.

We look at how Multi-choice can combat it and what the consequences are in SA.

THE GADGETS - HOW DOES IT WORK?
Illegal streaming devices allow users to access hundreds of channels via a subscription on a dodgy app. It’s a cheap way of getting all the shows you want. But you’re connecting an illegal device onto your home wifi network – a device that’s connected to global servers that you have no control over, that thousands of others have access to too.

THE APP – WAKA TV.net
It a more affordable — but illegal — alternative to DSTV.
WakaTV.net on Facebook advertised for R160 a month – it’s a Live TV and Video on Demand platform with more than 150 national and international channels, and 60,000 movies and series.
At this stage the app is only compatible with the following Android devices: TV Box, TV Stick, Skyworth, Android TV, Chromecast with Android TV, NO SMART TV’s or mobile devices.
UNDERCOVER ELEMENT
There is a shop in Ferndale – we’ll buy a streaming box, get the lowdown in the shop and sign up for subscription. We’ll come back for a confront.

TECH ELEMENT
Risk Diversion – they are an analysis company that will help us set up the unit at my place – they will explain how it works and what access we get. Filmed in a show and tell setting.

UNDERSTANDING THE BIGGER PICTURE
So we buy from a Reseller, that buys from a Dealer, that buys from a SuperDealer, that buys from the Owner of the Server – this server is usually overseas – the MultiChoice techie people have tracked some of these and will explain these networks to us. We interview Frikkie Jonker from MultiChoice’s Anti-Piracy Unit… We build it – as here somewhere in this building is a unit that operates in the shadows / under the radar, the staff members assigned to this team, call themselves agents, their identities often hidden, their tasks usually classified, it’s not a popular job.

Frikkie will explain how because piracy is not a priority crime in many countries – they’ve had to really get ahead of the scourge with technology and the by counter measures, they infiltrate these networks, gain access to their servers and they shut them down – one by one. They’ll show us how they shut down WAKA TV

CRITICISM / FLACK – WE LEAN INTO IT
But Pay TV in SA is so expensive – it is but paying in this case “goedkoop koop is duur-koop” – you’re opening yourself up to underground cyber crime networks. If you’re caught with these devices you could face serious charges.

Not a serious crime – we agree – but could make you vulnerable to cyber crime attacks

GLOBAL IMPACT / LEGALITY
We use Billy Petzer from the CSIR Cyber Crime Unit to set the stage of international Cyber crime and why this is not a good idea and explain how users make themselves vulnerable and to what.

IT MAYBE A SOFT CRIME – BUT YOU COULD STILL END UP BEHING BARS IN SOUTH AFRICA
Those convicted of Internet piracy in South Africa could face a fine of R5,000 or three years’ jail time, while repeat offenders could be fined R10,000 or face five years in jail.

According to the Copyright Act, selling and using these services is viewed as a criminal offence.
“Any device used to bypass subscription services or to access copyrighted content such as movies, series or sporting events is in contravention of our law and, as such, a criminal offence,” it reads.

It’s estimated that Piracy / Illegal Streaming costs the USA $173 Billion a year! The entertainment industry is massive, it employs millions of people directly and indirectly in sub-industries as well. Piracy impacts on the viability of the industry.

CONVICTIONS
There have been successful convictions against people selling these services in South Africa.
In the past year, Irdeto and MultiChoice saw the conviction of 2 perpetrators (Lee Whaley and Jordan Lee Mott) in relation to them pirating content. Lee Whaley was arrested by detectives from the Provincial Commercial Unit for the selling of Android TV Boxes and IPTV subscriptions in December 2019. The Android TV Box and IPTV subscriptions allowed access to premium copyright-protected content, including DStv content. While offenders in South Africa face fines of R5,000 to R10,000 or jail time of three to five years, punishments overseas can be much harsher. In May 2023, the Chesterfield Justice Centre in the UK sentenced five men to a combined 30 years’ jail time. The men were behind the IPTV service Flawless IPTV, which accumulated over 50,000 subscribers and an estimated £4.6 million in revenue, £3.7 million of which was profit.The profit was split unequally between six people — Mark Gould, Steven Gordon, Peter Jolley, Christopher Felvus, William Brown, and Zak Smith.

The amount of profit paid to each of the five sentenced perpetrators and their punishment is summarised below:
• Mark Gould — received £1.7 million profit. Sentenced to 11 years on two counts of conspiracy to defraud and contempt of court.
• Steven Gordon — received £1 million profit. Sentenced to five years and two months in prison on two counts of conspiracy to defraud and contempt of court.
• Peter Jolley — £773,000 profit. Sentenced to five years and two months in prison on two counts of conspiracy to defraud and money laundering
• Christopher Felvus — £164,500 profit. Sentenced to three years and 11 months in prison on two counts of conspiracy to defraud
• William Brown — £15,000 profit. Sentenced to four years and nine months on two counts of conspiracy to defraud, after pleading not guilty.

Zak Smith failed to appear in court, and a warrant was issued for his arrest.

INTERVIEWS / ELEMENTS
• UNDERCOVER – We buy a box
• TECH ELEMENT – We install it – RISK DIVERSION
• THE IMPACT – We interview Billy Petzer from the CSIR’s CYBER CRIME UNIT to understand global cyber crime networks at play
• THE SOUTH AFRICAN CONTEXT & GLOBAL STAGE – We interview Frikkie Jonker from MultiChoice’s Anti-Piracy Unit…
• CONFRONT

FINAL SCRIPT PIRACY

UPSOUND OF MOVIE -

VO: ……..PIRACY…….

Billions of Dollars…lost… lawless masterminds hiding in complex territories from those that hunt them to protect their bounties…..

PAUSE

LINK: I'm not talking about that kind of piracy.

CYBER SEQUENCE…..

VO: This is a different kind of theft.

LOUNGE SCENE – WATCHING TV – SWITCH OFF SCREEN
LINK: Online piracy. Illegally downloading and streaming copyrighted material.

VO: Pirated video material gets over 230 billion views globally every year….even here in South Africa… from Hollywood Blockbusters to ground-breaking local series, documentaries, news, sport, you name it…

VO: Dodgy streaming services account for more than 80% of global online piracy - these platforms are popular, cheap and in demand.

Frikkie Jonker, heads Multichoice’s Broadcasting Cyber Security Anti-Piracy Division.

MASA: The reality is PayTV in SA is very expensive and this could be tempting
FRIKKIE: To maintain a legal, you know, entertainment industry, it costs money //. Pirates pays nothing. They pay nothing.

VO: The US entertainment industry loses as much as $70 billion dollars every year. Meaning not just less profit for big corporates, but significant job losses in an industry employing hundreds of thousands of people.

FRIKKIE: These dealers don't pay any any rights holders, any cents. I mean, no money, is paid for the actors, for the songwriters, for the sportsmen, nobody.

VO: Piracy undercuts the premiums, that pay for broadcast rights to bring viewers big sporting events and blockbusters.

FRIKKIE: it is millions upon billion dollars. I mean, if that revenue stream is not there anymore, soccer will not exist anymore. Movies will not exist anymore.

LINK: It all starts with a good deal. I mean, a really good deal. Let me explain.

LAPTOP SCENE – WALK IN, SIT DOWN, WALK OUT
LINK: Cheap streaming services are available on the net and you get a lot of bang for your buck starting at 160 rand a month, you get promised access to hundreds of international and local channels and streaming services all in one low, low fee. And some resellers even offer in-person contact.

DSTV CUSTOMER CENTRE SCENE – WALK IN & OUT
LINK: You can even visit their shops, but it won't be in a legitimate, swanky service center.

DODGY SHOP SCENE – WALK IN & OUT
LINK: This is where you come…..

VO: Meet Tawanda – he’s a friendly reseller. Sometimes he operates from this shop and other times he’s on the road, taking his services to the people.

Apart from a smart TV or streaming device - you’d also need a specific app. The piracy involves several other steps. And, you guessed it ...... Tawanda helps with all of them.

While the device cost R450, the first month’s subscription was all of 250 bucks.

HIDDEN CAMERA.
AGENT: And this will give me all the channels - supersport?
TAWANDA: All the Supersports or… It’s even better than DSTV, because it’s got other channels that are not on DSTV //I’ve actually cancelled my Netflix, my DSTV, my Showmax, everything – I only have ****

VO: More from Tawanda later. First, we wanted to know how it all works. Darryl Nyawasha is an IT specialist.

DARYL: This TV box is a plug and play device// the application is installed and all we need to do now is connect to the wifi so that it's on the Internet and then we are ready to go.
MASA: That took less than 30 seconds. It was very quick.
DARYL: Yes. It's very simple.
MASA: Voila. //So what do we have? Of course Mnet. All the DSTV channels, National Geographic, Nickelodeon, something for kids, SABC. Oh, it's a lot of sports channels // do we know where it's all coming from?
DARYL: Just by looking at it, it's difficult to tell, but there are ways to figure out exactly where this data is coming from//

TWO BEATS

VO: But at a fraction of the price, the content is definitely not coming from legitimate enterprises like Multichoice.

FRIKKIE: If you use content that you actually don't get from a legitimate provider, actually, you're stealing something that doesn't belong to you.
MASA: Some South Africans would say it's not really stealing.
FRIKKIE: It's definitely stealing. If you go to a dealership and your dream car is a Mercedes Benz, and you go you climb into that car, you actually drive off without paying it, // it's theft. You actually stole something that doesn't belong to you.

VO: But this doesn’t worry resellers like Tawanda….

HIDDEN CAMERA UPSOUND
TAWANDA: Don’t worry, no one will catch you…
AGENT: you haven’t had any problems?
TAWANDA: No, don’t worry. I’ve got more than a hundred people now
AGENT: More than 100!
TAWANDA: And the numbers keep on growing.
AGENT: No one got caught yet?
TAWANDA: No… (shakes head)

TWO BEATS

VO: But online piracy is cyber crime. And illegally consuming content, often unwittingly opens the door to a whole other world that could put users directly at risk.

BILLY: There is no such thing as a free lunch. // You are almost like you are paying for it in some other way.

VO: Billy Petzer is from the Cyber Crime Systems at the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research.

BILLY: it's safe to assume that these are people providing these platforms have malicious intentions and not necessarily the altruistic Robin Hood in the streaming community that just want to provide a cheap or free service.

VO: Complying with legislation and safeguarding user security are not usually top priorities for Illegal streaming platforms.

BILLY: it’s been found in many of these streaming boxes that they have backdoors embedded in them that can essentially give an attacker unmitigated access to your home network.

VO: IN OTHER WORDS, they have access to everything you do online - social media, email, banking even your cctv cameras - everything that’s linked to your wifi.

We're back with Daryl, an IT specialist who tests systems for weaknesses. He analysed the streaming device Tawanda supplied, to establish if there were any real risks.

DARYL: It was actually possible to compromise the device itself with almost no effort. And then we saw that the device itself was connecting to hundreds of IP addresses all across the world.
MASA: This is all happening while you're watching your favourite show. Illegally.
DARYL: Correct.

VO: An IP address is the unique identifying number assigned to every device connected to the internet.

MASA: I'm seeing a lot of flags. The South African flag, the German flag, USA flag.
DARYL: Essentially, that flag represents // where the data you’re watching is coming from. So if you're watching program// hosted on a server in Germany. We would then have a German flag and the IP address.
MASA: So what we're dealing with here is not one big mother server.
DARYL: No. So it's several servers sitting across the world // but exactly who it is, is difficult to know.

ADD PAUSE
** MOVE UPT SOUND EFFECT
VO: Working with international law enforcement, Jonker’s teams investigate illegal streaming syndicates from the small time resellers, to the superdealers, and ultimately the server owners.

FRIKKIE: The person makes the most profit at the end of the day. is the the people that sit outside of the African continent in Africa. We are tracking pirates across the world. From JHB to China, from China to the Netherlands. Everywhere it is syndicates, international crime syndicates that manage these types of operations.

VO: But low-level resellers downplay the risk.

HIDDEN CAMERA
AGENT: They're not going to catch me. I don't want to go to prison.
TAWANDA: Don’t worry, don’t worry //
AGENT: So they won't catch me. But it's legal.
TAWANDA: It's not legal.
AGENT: But no one's going to come for me.
TAWANDA No. If you're paying a subscription, if anybody comes to you, you direct them where you're paying.

LINK: At the end of the day these streaming apps are not legal - and the money collected are essentially the proceeds of crime - but I wonder if the people who are selling these devices see it that way….

MASA: I’m from Carte Blanche //what you’re doing is illegal.
TAWANDA - No, I don’t know
MASA - you don’t know
TAWANDA - I sell TVs and smart TV boxes.

VO: We refreshed his memory and showed him our hidden camera footage…

MASA - WHO IS THIS over here
TAWANDA - that’s me….
MASA - you’ve done this subscription for over 100 people already - have you told them it’s illegal and that they can be criminally charged
TAWANDA - SIGHS

VO: ….Tawanda was running out of words….

MASA - This is illegal - you know that. Ah Tawanda - you know -
TAWANDA - i can help you if you want, but stop pressing you agenda
MASA - Let me help you understand something, I have you on camera admitting to know it’s illegal.
TAWANDA - This is someone trying to make a sale it’s the language of a sales person

TAWANDA - I now know it’s illegal //
MASA - Are you going to stop Tawanda
TAWANDA - I can stop now - i don’t need this kind of stress on me already.

VO: But Tawanda is just one of many middlemen resellers, pushing one of many illegal streaming apps. And while it’s an illicit market that needs constant policing - the reality is it's not a priority crime.

LINK: // So it's left up to content producers and providers to combat it.

VO: Using specialist software, Multichoice remotely shuts down its content on illegal streaming services.

FRIKKIE: We identified our channel on this pirate platform that was played out, // with tools that we utilize. And as you can see, it's frozen right now. This is what the customer will see now - the content is gone.
MASA: Just like that?
FRIKKIE: Just like that. All our teams on the African continent has got this tool available for them and we can actually do it. 24 seven.

VO: But it could get worse than just losing your connection, online piracy could actually land you behind bars - even as just a user.

DARYL: The issue is people think that they won't get caught and people think that everyone is doing it. But we see it time and time again where one of these operations at the surface gets seized and they're able to actually pull everyone who's communicated with the server, even for the last five years// you could be prosecuted for consuming that content illegally and it would break both local and international laws as well.

VO: And don’t forget, even if you aren’t the suspect, you could still be the victim.

BILLY: You don't know who you are actually giving access into your home network. // even if you think you have nothing to hide, you still have something of value, something that can be stolen.

VO: Because in a cyber world ruled by criminals, the true risks…are often masked.









 
PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: Illegal streaming services get you so much more than cheap access to your favourite shows - it opens you up the dark world of cyber crime.

BILLY: There is no such thing as a free lunch. // You are almost like you are paying for it in some other way.

VO: With online piracy, you could go from user to suspect to victim in a matter of clicks..


PROMO 2
VO: Alternative entertainment streaming services are cheap, in demand and a little shady…

TAWANDA: Don’t worry, no one will catch you…

VO: But that’s not completely true….

MASA: I’m from Carte Blanche //what you’re doing is illegal.

VO: Don’t miss this investigation into online piracy.



PROMO 3
VO: Online piracy is tempting. It’s easy and it’s cheap. But it’s also illegal.

FRIKKIE: you're stealing something that doesn't belong to you.

VO: But even worse, illegal streaming opens you up to a cyber world ruled by criminals, where the true risks…are often masked.

metadata.Summary: We’re not taking Jack Sparrow robbing ships at sea, we’re talking about illegal use or reproduction of copyrighted material. It can feel like a bit of a non-event in the South Africa Crime context… 70+ people get taken out every day. But it’s not just about copying DVDs and downloading movies of torrent sites… piracy IS cyber crime…. You think it’s nothing and it’s big corporates making a noise, but it’s actually much more sinister and it has a real impact much closer to home, actually right in your home. This story looks at the evolution of piracy.
metadata.Further information: THE FOCUS OF THIS STORY Technology, the fact that while piracy is a soft crime – it is cyber crime and it opens you up to much wider darker illegal activity unwittingly – it’s not just cheap TV channels that you’re getting. We look at how Multi-choice can combat it and what the consequences are in SA. THE GADGETS - HOW DOES IT WORK? Illegal streaming devices allow users to access hundreds of channels via a subscription on a dodgy app. It’s a cheap way of getting all the shows you want. But you’re connecting an illegal device onto your home wifi network – a device that’s connected to global servers that you have no control over, that thousands of others have access to too. THE APP – WAKA TV.net It a more affordable — but illegal — alternative to DSTV. WakaTV.net on Facebook advertised for R160 a month – it’s a Live TV and Video on Demand platform with more than 150 national and international channels, and 60,000 movies and series. At this stage the app is only compatible with the following Android devices: TV Box, TV Stick, Skyworth, Android TV, Chromecast with Android TV, NO SMART TV’s or mobile devices. UNDERCOVER ELEMENT There is a shop in Ferndale – we’ll buy a streaming box, get the lowdown in the shop and sign up for subscription. We’ll come back for a confront. TECH ELEMENT Risk Diversion – they are an analysis company that will help us set up the unit at my place – they will explain how it works and what access we get. Filmed in a show and tell setting. UNDERSTANDING THE BIGGER PICTURE So we buy from a Reseller, that buys from a Dealer, that buys from a SuperDealer, that buys from the Owner of the Server – this server is usually overseas – the MultiChoice techie people have tracked some of these and will explain these networks to us. We interview Frikkie Jonker from MultiChoice’s Anti-Piracy Unit… We build it – as here somewhere in this building is a unit that operates in the shadows / under the radar, the staff members assigned to this team, call themselves agents, their identities often hidden, their tasks usually classified, it’s not a popular job. Frikkie will explain how because piracy is not a priority crime in many countries – they’ve had to really get ahead of the scourge with technology and the by counter measures, they infiltrate these networks, gain access to their servers and they shut them down – one by one. They’ll show us how they shut down WAKA TV CRITICISM / FLACK – WE LEAN INTO IT But Pay TV in SA is so expensive – it is but paying in this case “goedkoop koop is duur-koop” – you’re opening yourself up to underground cyber crime networks. If you’re caught with these devices you could face serious charges. Not a serious crime – we agree – but could make you vulnerable to cyber crime attacks GLOBAL IMPACT / LEGALITY We use Billy Petzer from the CSIR Cyber Crime Unit to set the stage of international Cyber crime and why this is not a good idea and explain how users make themselves vulnerable and to what. IT MAYBE A SOFT CRIME – BUT YOU COULD STILL END UP BEHING BARS IN SOUTH AFRICA Those convicted of Internet piracy in South Africa could face a fine of R5,000 or three years’ jail time, while repeat offenders could be fined R10,000 or face five years in jail. According to the Copyright Act, selling and using these services is viewed as a criminal offence. “Any device used to bypass subscription services or to access copyrighted content such as movies, series or sporting events is in contravention of our law and, as such, a criminal offence,” it reads. It’s estimated that Piracy / Illegal Streaming costs the USA $173 Billion a year! The entertainment industry is massive, it employs millions of people directly and indirectly in sub-industries as well. Piracy impacts on the viability of the industry. CONVICTIONS There have been successful convictions against people selling these services in South Africa. In the past year, Irdeto and MultiChoice saw the conviction of 2 perpetrators (Lee Whaley and Jordan Lee Mott) in relation to them pirating content. Lee Whaley was arrested by detectives from the Provincial Commercial Unit for the selling of Android TV Boxes and IPTV subscriptions in December 2019. The Android TV Box and IPTV subscriptions allowed access to premium copyright-protected content, including DStv content. While offenders in South Africa face fines of R5,000 to R10,000 or jail time of three to five years, punishments overseas can be much harsher. In May 2023, the Chesterfield Justice Centre in the UK sentenced five men to a combined 30 years’ jail time. The men were behind the IPTV service Flawless IPTV, which accumulated over 50,000 subscribers and an estimated £4.6 million in revenue, £3.7 million of which was profit.The profit was split unequally between six people — Mark Gould, Steven Gordon, Peter Jolley, Christopher Felvus, William Brown, and Zak Smith. The amount of profit paid to each of the five sentenced perpetrators and their punishment is summarised below: • Mark Gould — received £1.7 million profit. Sentenced to 11 years on two counts of conspiracy to defraud and contempt of court. • Steven Gordon — received £1 million profit. Sentenced to five years and two months in prison on two counts of conspiracy to defraud and contempt of court. • Peter Jolley — £773,000 profit. Sentenced to five years and two months in prison on two counts of conspiracy to defraud and money laundering • Christopher Felvus — £164,500 profit. Sentenced to three years and 11 months in prison on two counts of conspiracy to defraud • William Brown — £15,000 profit. Sentenced to four years and nine months on two counts of conspiracy to defraud, after pleading not guilty. Zak Smith failed to appear in court, and a warrant was issued for his arrest.
